name: E137
summary: E137 operated at SLAC, Menlo Park, California. Originally a historical beam experiment for light weakly coupled particles, it is included because of later dark-matter reinterpretations.
detection_principle: Electrons striking a target produce weakly coupled particles that traverse shielding and generate distant electromagnetic showers. Modern light-dark-matter reinterpretations model mediator production of dark matter followed by scattering on detector electrons.

status.label: Historical experiment taking data in 1980–1982; the 2014 dark-matter reinterpretation does not imply a restart

results.summary: Analysis of historical E137 data constrains sub-GeV dark matter and light mediators, with model and acceptance dependence.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered. This record includes reinterpretations of historical data in new models. A reinterpretation paper's publication year is not the apparatus operating year, and the original experiment may primarily have targeted neutrinos, axions or other light particles.
